scope.title: Work done by a variable force; signed F–x area and ideal spring work
included_core: Force varies with position along one straight axis
Signed area under F_parallel–x: rectangles, triangles, trapezia
Correct sign when force changes sign
Why endpoint force times distance is generally wrong
Work by and against ideal spring between two nonzero extensions
Crossing natural length x=0 and reverse-direction checks
excluded: General nonlinear force curves with exact non-elementary areas
Claims that all forces besides spring vanish without declared assumption

beyond_grade9.notation: ∫F dx — beyond Grade 9, given; never required, used, or tested

scope.link_to_prior_tile: WEP-01 provides force/body/frame, sign of constant-force work and signed summation.

shared_inferential_jump: For work by a specified force on a specified body in a fixed frame, replace the constant-force rectangle with the signed area of its force-component–position graph over the directed motion, combine the above- and below-axis pieces, and use an ideal spring’s straight-line graph to compare work by and against the spring between any two deformations.

truth_sources.use: Work on chosen body and sign of constant-force component; WEP-01 prerequisite

conventions.statement: Specify the physical target body, force agent, one-dimensional ground (inertial) frame, observation interval and force component along a fixed +x axis.
Use x in metres as signed spring-end or body position; for springs x=0 is the natural length, x>0 is extension and x<0 is compression; k>0 has units N/m.
The plotted F_x(x) must be the force component ON the target body along the chosen x direction. Motion between supplied endpoints follows the stated direction. No unlisted force is presumed absent.

For a graph composed of horizontal and straight sloping pieces, compute work by adding the signed rectangle/triangle/trapezium areas between initial and final x. Horizontal-axis crossings split the pieces.
For motion toward increasing x, graph area above the x-axis is positive, below negative; for traversal from x2 back to x1 with the same F(x), every segment sign reverses. Force-area units N·m=J.
A varying force does not generally do W=F(x1)(x2−x1) or W=F(x2)(x2−x1); these use one height for the whole graph. F_average Δx is exact for a linear graph with F_average=(F1+F2)/2.

Ideal spring is massless for work-account purposes, obeys F_spring on attached body=−kx throughout the stated range, and is anchored at one end; its graph is a straight line through the origin with negative slope.
Spring work between x1 and x2 equals W_spring=½k(x1²−x2²); ideal elastic-energy change ΔU_s=½k(x2²−x1²) with U_s(0)=0. Work by the spring is −ΔU_s.

“Work against the spring” is work by an external balancing agent on the spring-attached body, exactly −W_spring only for quasi-static, negligible-friction displacement with no net kinetic-energy change and no other along-axis work.

The force graph may be used to compute the work by one named force even if friction or other forces are present. To infer overall energy/kinetic change one must account for work by every acting force.
Elementary signed areas are exact for explicitly horizontal or linear straight-line graph portions. General curved graphs need additional approximations or higher-level methods, not required here.

microtopic.title: From changing force to signed work: geometric F–x area and ideal spring
microtopic.badge_reason: Learners must translate a changing force graph to a signed area, break a zero crossing into distinct regions, and separate spring work from external work; these transitions are easy to misread as force-times-distance.
entry_assumptions: Can name the force agent and target body and distinguish displacement from distance (WEP-01).
Can choose a right-positive 1D axis and identify initial/final coordinates in a fixed ground inertial frame.
Can use W=F_parallel s=Fs cosθ for a constant force and identify positive/negative work (WEP-01).
Can add signed numbers and use metre, newton and joule units.
Can calculate rectangle, triangle, and trapezium areas and interpret slope of a straight line without calculus.
Can solve simple one-step algebra, square a decimal and convert cm to m.
Knows Newton’s laws enough to distinguish force agents and that balanced forces can allow slow nearly constant-speed motion.
No prior spring-energy formula assumed; the ideal spring force law is introduced and then constructed geometrically.
microtopic.inferential_jump: For work by a specified force on a specified body in a fixed frame, replace the constant-force rectangle with the signed area of its force-component–position graph over the directed motion, combine the above- and below-axis pieces, and use an ideal spring’s straight-line graph to compare work by and against the spring between any two deformations.

teaching_path.action: Choose the force acting on the target body, inertial frame, signed position x, and the ordered endpoints; label F_x rather than an unsigned force magnitude.
teaching_path.why_valid: Work is about a named agent/body and displacement in a declared frame; F_x sign must match this axis.

teaching_path.action: Connect the WEP-01 constant-force case to a flat F_x–x graph: its rectangular area has magnitude |F_x|·|Δx| with sign from force and traversal.
teaching_path.why_valid: A constant force has the same height at every position; a rectangle encodes the earlier relation.

teaching_path.action: For a linearly varying force segment, use trapezium area width × mean of endpoint signed heights; alternatively split into rectangle and triangle.
teaching_path.why_valid: Straight-line height changes uniformly: the rectangle-plus-triangle formula equals the average-height trapezium.

teaching_path.action: Split a graph at a crossing of F_x=0; treat above-axis and below-axis regions separately and add their signed areas.
teaching_path.why_valid: The direction of force relative to displacement changes at an axis crossing, so geometric magnitudes cannot all be added positively.

teaching_path.action: Contrast endpoint F×distance with the actual trapezium for a sloped segment. Endpoint multiplication gives the wrong area unless the force is constant or a special coincidence occurs.
teaching_path.why_valid: One endpoint height cannot represent changing force over the interval; the graph contains the missing change.

teaching_path.action: Specify an ideal Hooke spring, the undeformed reference x=0, and an attached body; distinguish restoring spring force −kx from the balancing applied force +kx.
teaching_path.why_valid: A stretched spring pulls back, a compressed spring pushes out; the two named agents have opposite forces.

teaching_path.action: For an ideal spring, use the straight F_spring=−kx graph; determine the signed triangle from 0 to x and subtract two endpoint triangles to obtain W_spring(x1→x2)=½k(x1²−x2²).
teaching_path.why_valid: Each endpoint triangle magnitude is ½·|x|·k|x|=½kx²; directed signed subtraction handles both stretching and compression.

teaching_path.action: During slow ideal stretching, work by the balancing agent is the opposite of spring work and equals the increase of U_s=½kx². State the no-friction and no-net-change-in-K conditions.
teaching_path.why_valid: With no kinetic change or additional along-axis transfer, the applied and spring works cancel; potential rises on stretching from equilibrium.

teaching_path.action: Reverse an interval in an unchanged F_x(x) field; the signed work changes sign. Check a zero-net-work case with nonzero force on different portions and no invented total-force assumptions.
teaching_path.why_valid: Reversing the direction swaps sign of each directed area. Positive and negative pieces can cancel without making force or motion zero.

teaching_path.action: Check units and scope: newtons times metres produce joules; compare individual-force work and net work; curved graphs are not exactly one elementary trapezium.
teaching_path.why_valid: Dimensional and domain tests catch wrong heights, wrong body, sign and invalid approximation.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: For varying force, multiply the force at the start by the whole distance.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: A graph rises from 2 N to 8 N over 3 m. Would using 2×3 reproduce the geometric trapezium?
misconceptions.repair: Compare the single rectangle to the trapezium; draw the extra triangular part rather than reusing one endpoint height.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Every geometric area is positive, so positive and negative force regions add as positive magnitudes.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: A graph spends equal signed triangular areas above and below the axis. What is the signed total work?
misconceptions.repair: Write one signed row per interval, then add algebraically; area below the axis contributes negative work in a rightward traversal.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: The spring always does negative work, even while returning toward the natural length.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: An initially extended spring pulls the body left while the body moves left. What is the spring-work sign?
misconceptions.repair: Identify the actual direction of motion relative to restoring force; verify with W_spring=½k(x1²−x2²).

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Work done against the spring is the same signed work as work done by the spring.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: In a quasistatic stretch from 0.05 m to 0.15 m, do the spring force and applied pulling force have the same direction?
misconceptions.repair: Name the agent for each force. Under explicitly frictionless, quasistatic conditions, external balancing force is opposite the spring force.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: For a spring extended from x1 to x2, work only depends on x2, as though the stretch always starts at zero.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: If a spring already starts extended, can a new stretch cost the entire zero-to-final stored energy again?
misconceptions.repair: Subtract the initial triangle from the final triangle, or compute the signed trapezium between x1 and x2.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: At a force-axis crossing, motion must stop or total work must be zero.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: If F_x passes through 0 at one position while the body continues, must the total area on both sides cancel?
misconceptions.repair: Distinguish the instantaneous force value from the area accumulated over the full displacement; compare actual signed regions.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Reversing motion leaves work by a given position-dependent force unchanged because the graph is unchanged.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: A body moves from x=1 to 3 and then back from 3 to 1 with the same F(x); are the two works equal in sign?
misconceptions.repair: Reverse the directed interval, not the graph; every signed contribution changes sign.

microtopic.research_contribution: Enrichment from OpenStax work–position and ideal spring references; original no-calculus rectangle/triangle/trapezium constructions, sign-changing counterexample and explicit external-work conditions.

predict.prompt: A body moves right while one force acting on it grows and later changes sign according to a force–position graph. Can one initial force magnitude multiplied by total travel reliably describe work for the entire interval? Make a prediction and give a reason.
predict.defensible_answer: No; the graph contains changing signed force contributions. A single initial magnitude cannot represent a variable force or sign change.

attempt.produces: Before seeing the model, declare one named target body and force agent, fixed ground frame, positive-x axis, ordered position endpoints and graph segments. Produce an original rectangle/triangle/trapezium signed-work ledger, explain a force-axis crossing, and compare work by an ideal spring and an external balancing agent between two stated nonzero endpoints, listing assumptions and units. State one check under reversed traversal and explain when endpoint F×s fails.
attempt.model_response: Fix body, agent and frame and read each F_x(x) segment for the directed interval. Constant regions contribute signed rectangles, linear regions trapezia or rectangle-plus-triangle, splitting at a force-axis crossing; sum signed contributions in J. An ideal spring has F_spring=−kx, so W_spring=½k(x1²−x2²), not −½kx2² unless x1=0. Only under slow, frictionless balance with no other along-axis work does external agent do −W_spring; reversed traversal in the unchanged force law changes sign. An endpoint force multiplied by total displacement generally misses graph area.

rubric.criterion: Names body/agent, inertial frame, fixed +x and ordered endpoints before accounting.
rubric.evidence_of: One agent-to-body force component plotted against body position in the chosen ground frame.

rubric.criterion: Builds signed region ledger from elementary graph shapes including a force-axis crossing.
rubric.evidence_of: Rectangle/triangle/trapezium pieces with above/below work signs and a correct signed total.

rubric.criterion: Distinguishes work by spring from work by a slowly balancing external agent across nonzero endpoint deformations.
rubric.evidence_of: F_spring=−kx, initial/final extension values, opposite work signs only with explicit balance/no-friction conditions.

rubric.criterion: Gives units, reverse-direction check and explains why endpoint force times distance may fail.
rubric.evidence_of: N·m=J; reversed directed interval changes work sign; variable force needs the graph rather than one endpoint rectangle.

accepted: A labelled one-force signed-area ledger with separate pieces and a correctly conditional spring/external comparison.
rejected: The force at x1 times the whole distance is always work, and the spring’s work equals the whole final ½kx2². Incorrect: varying force needs signed graph area, and two nonzero spring endpoint energies must be compared.

route.ask: Whose displacement and which one force is being accounted for?
route.why_this_ask: Fixes owner and frame before solving geometry.

route.ask: Which graph regions have different heights or lie on different sides of zero force?
route.why_this_ask: Elicits representation choice instead of giving a sign rule first.

route.ask: Can each region be drawn as a rectangle, triangle or trapezium?
route.why_this_ask: Prompts no-calculus work construction.

route.ask: What changes when the ideal spring begins already stretched?
route.why_this_ask: Makes initial stored deformation relevant before calculating a difference.

route.ask: What condition is required for external work against a spring to be the exact opposite of spring work?
route.why_this_ask: Learner checks assumptions rather than silently borrowing a conservation result.

route.ask: What independent reversal or units test catches a sign error?
route.why_this_ask: Requires a self-check on the learner-owned result.

reconstruct.differs_from_teaching_path: A explains geometric accumulation and spring endpoints directly; B begins with choosing body/graph partitions, asks learner to construct the sign and conditional work comparison, then reveals closure.

boundary_test.prompt: A body moves right through an interval in which an acting force is positive on one portion and equally negative in signed-area magnitude on another. Could this force do zero net work even while it acts and the body moves? Explain the status of motion.
boundary_test.answer: Yes. The signed positive and negative work contributions cancel to zero. Motion and nonzero force occur on the portions; zero net work by this force does not require speed to vanish or imply that total work of all forces is zero.
boundary_test.confirms: Distinguishes signed work of a named force from force presence, displacement and the net work of all forces.

exit_task.prompt: An ideal anchored spring of k=60 N/m, negligible mass, operates on a horizontal frictionless track. Its attached block moves from x=+0.10 m to x=+0.40 m at nearly constant low speed under a balancing pull in the stationary ground frame (no other along-track forces). Compute the work by the spring and by the pull with a signed trapezium or endpoint triangles, show the spring energy increase, check signs and units. Then state whether an additional separate varying force would require its own graph-area calculation.

answer.summary: The spring does −4.5 J; slow balancing pull does +4.5 J; ΔU_s=+4.5 J; any separate force must be accounted for separately.
reasoning: Spring force on block is −kx; at .10 m it is −6 N and at .40 m −24 N; Δx=+.30 m.
Trapezium area [(−6−24)/2]×(.30)=−4.5 J is work by the spring.
By endpoint triangles: U_i=½(60)(.10²)=0.3 J; U_f=½(60)(.40²)=4.8 J; ΔU=+4.5 J and W_spring=−ΔU.
With a slow balancing pull and no other along-track work, W_pull=+4.5 J.
A separate force has its own work; its force–position graph would require additional signed areas, and full net work would sum all contributing forces.
answer.check: For further stretching the restoring force opposes the positive displacement; spring work negative, pull positive; N·m=J. The difference of endpoint triangles (4.8−0.3)=4.5 J matches the trapezium.
acceptable_alternatives: Rectangle-plus-triangle yielding −4.5 J for spring and +4.5 J for balancing pull.

relation.equation: For increasing x, W_force = sum of signed geometric areas of elementary graph pieces: rectangle FΔx; straight-line trapezium [(F_start+F_end)/2]Δx. For decreasing x reverse the sign. Ideal spring F_spring=−kx; W_spring(x1→x2)=½k(x1²−x2²); work against spring = −W_spring only under stated balancing conditions.
model_assumptions: Named force on named target body, with one consistent inertial ground frame and one signed x-axis.
Graph vertical ordinate is signed component F_x(x) in newtons, horizontal is x in metres.
For exact geometry each segment is constant or linear; if curve nonlinear, these shapes are approximations only.
Work as signed area taken over directed interval; sign reversal for motion to decreasing x.
Ideal linear Hooke spring with positive k and equilibrium x=0 within elastic range; no hysteresis/plasticity.
For external-work-as-negative-spring-work, slow quasi-static movement, negligible friction and other along-x forces, no change in kinetic energy.
Computation is work of an individual force; frictionlessness is NOT needed for that individual-force integral-by-area; net work requires inclusion of other forces.
relation.axis_and_sign: Rightward positive. When x increases, region above F_x=0 counts positive, region below negative. When x decreases, reverse each sign. For spring x>0 stretch, x<0 compression, F_spring=−kx.
relation.physical_interpretation: Changing forces do different amounts of work over different locations. Net work of one named force is not determined by one endpoint force. A linear spring stores ½kx² of elastic energy relative to its natural length; the spring-force work is minus the change of that stored energy.
checks: Constant F graph reduces to one rectangle, matching WEP-01.
Equal positive and negative signed areas cancel even though force and motion exist.
Reversing the interval with the same F_x(x) reverses the work sign.
For a spring x1=x2, work is zero for an immediate unchanged endpoint (the same endpoints also give zero net spring work for a reversible out-and-back excursion).
For spring stretch x2>x1≥0, W_spring<0; for release toward 0, W_spring>0.
k>0 and all endpoint positions use metres; two spring energy terms are subtracted for x1≠0.
External work against a spring is not automatically minus spring work with friction, acceleration or extra along-axis forces.

proposed_extension_candidate.canon_library_excluded: Current repository WEP bucket excluded elastic spring and variable-force work, although the Owner’s frozen syllabus now requires WEP-02.

core1a.title: WEP-02 — Why changing force means signed graph area

ordered_blocks.show: Grade 9: one named varying force on a body in one ground frame, signed graph areas and ideal spring between arbitrary endpoints.

questions.title: Rectangle plus triangle on a rising force graph
questions.setup: Ground-frame block moves right from x=0 to 5 m; the named horizontal force ON it is +2 N for 0≤x≤3 m, then rises linearly from +2 to +6 N between x=3 and 5 m. The graph is exact and other forces are irrelevant to this one-force work calculation.

reasoning: Choose block as target, right-positive ground frame, and directed travel x=0→5 m. The plotted F_x is this named force on the block.
On 0→3 m the height is 2 N, so rectangular work = 3 m × 2 N = +6 J.
On 3→5 m make a rectangle at 2 N with work +4 J and a triangle of width 2 m and extra height 4 N with work +4 J.
Their sum is +6+4+4 = +14 J; equivalently the latter trapezium is [(2+6)/2]×2=+8 J.
Using the starting force 2 N over the entire 5 m would give 10 J, which omits the growing-force region.
answer.summary: Work of the specified varying force is +14 J.
answer.check: F_x remains positive; the answer must be positive and has N·m=J units.

questions.title: A changing-sign force during one motion
questions.setup: A puck moves right on a track from x=0 to x=4 m. A named horizontal force on the puck decreases linearly from +6 N at x=0 to 0 at x=2 m, then to −4 N at x=4 m. The puck’s continued rightward motion is stipulated; no claim about net force is made.

reasoning: The target is the puck; ground frame +x right, motion x=0→4. The graph crosses F_x=0 at x=2.
First triangle lies above the axis: +½(2 m)(6 N)=+6 J.
Second triangle lies below the axis: −½(2 m)(4 N)=−4 J.
Add signed areas: W_this_force = +6−4 = +2 J. At x=2 the instantaneous force component is 0, not the accumulated work.
The work of all forces or final speed cannot be inferred without knowing other forces and initial speed.
answer.summary: One specified force does +2 J even though its sign changes during the motion.
answer.check: The positive region is larger than the negative by 2 J; both force and motion may exist when F_x crosses zero.

questions.title: Below-axis trapezium
questions.setup: A body travels to the right from x=1 to x=4 m. One named horizontal force on the body varies linearly from −2 N to −6 N. Use a fixed ground frame.

reasoning: Fix target body and +x right. The displacement is 3 m right.
Since both force-component heights are negative, the trapezium is below the axis.
Magnitude of area = [(2+6)/2] N × 3 m = 12 J.
Attach negative sign for force opposite increasing-x displacement: W=−12 J.
If the body retraced 4→1 m through the unchanged field, work of the same force would be +12 J.
answer.summary: The named force does −12 J for the rightward interval.
answer.check: Dimensions N·m=J; reverse traversal gives +12 J.

questions.title: Stretch an ideal spring between two nonzero extensions
questions.setup: Ideal anchored spring with k=200 N/m is attached to a sliding block. In the stationary ground frame the end is slowly stretched from x1=+0.10 m to x2=+0.30 m, where x is signed deformation from natural length. Assume negligible friction, no other along-axis force and negligible change in kinetic energy.

reasoning: For x>0 the restoring force of the spring on the block is F_spring=−kx, from −20 N to −60 N over Δx=+0.20 m.
The force–position trapezium is entirely below the axis. W_spring = [(−20−60)/2]×0.20=−8 J.
Equivalently the full 0→0.30 m triangle is ½(200)(0.30²)=9 J, and the prior 0→0.10 m triangle is 1 J: spring work for the additional stretch is −(9−1)=−8 J.
To maintain slow equilibrium, an external pull is +kx at every point. Its work is +8 J, the opposite of spring work in this specified model.
The increase in stored spring potential energy ΔU_s = ½k(x2²−x1²)=+8 J, with U_s(0)=0.
answer.summary: Spring does −8 J; slow ideal external agent does +8 J; stored spring energy increases by +8 J.
answer.check: The final deformation is larger, so the spring’s restoring work during further stretching is negative; the zero-to-final answer 9 J is not the interval answer.

questions.title: Compress-to-stretch traversal crosses natural length
questions.setup: An ideal spring k=100 N/m is attached to a mass guided without friction in the ground frame. Its signed deformation changes from x1=−0.20 m (compression) to x2=+0.10 m (stretch), while the mass follows this directed motion. Calculate work done by spring only; no assumption of slow balanced external motion is made.

reasoning: For x=−0.20, F_spring=+20 N; at x=0 force is 0; at x=+0.10, F_spring=−10 N.
From −0.20 to 0, force and rightward displacement align: positive triangle area ½(0.20)(20)=+2 J.
From 0 to +0.10, restoring force opposes rightward motion: negative triangle area −½(0.10)(10)=−0.5 J.
Signed spring-work total is +2−0.5=+1.5 J.
Cross-check W_spring=½(100)[(−0.20)²−(+0.10)²]=50(0.04−0.01)=+1.5 J. Other-force work is not claimed.
answer.summary: Spring does +1.5 J across compression-to-stretch motion.
answer.check: Initial spring stored energy is 2 J; final is 0.5 J, so spring work is +1.5 J.

questions.title: Endpoint-force multiplication fails when slope is nonzero
questions.setup: On a rightward displacement x=0→4 m, a specified force on a body rises in a straight line from +1 N to +5 N; no other force is being calculated.

reasoning: The fixed +x ground frame gives Δx=4 m and both signed heights positive.
A force that changes with position does not keep either endpoint height over the whole interval.
The exact signed trapezium is (1+5)/2×4=+12 J.
Initial-height rectangle gives 1×4=4 J; final-height rectangle gives 5×4=20 J; neither is the graph’s area.
Here only, the mean of the endpoint forces is exactly the mean force because F(x) is a straight line; +3 N×4 m=+12 J.
answer.summary: Actual work +12 J; initial- or final-force times displacement generally fails.
answer.check: The trapezium lies between its 4-J and 20-J endpoint rectangles, giving a plausibility check.

scope_guards: No calculus anywhere in learner task or worked route; only exact rectangular, triangular and trapezial graph pieces.
Spring forces and work are assigned to agents correctly. Quasistatic external-agent work requires explicit conditions.
Figures are described as authored specs and never claimed to be actual exam graphics.

core1b.title: WEP-02 — Decide graph areas before revealing the construction

ordered_blocks.text: WEP-02: changing force graphs and ideal spring contexts; commit to each analysis before revealing calculations.

ordered_blocks.resolution: Allowlist only; do not project the entire bucket.conventions.

predict.prompt: A body moves to the right along a straight track while a named force on it changes with position. A graph shows the force component as a horizontal line followed by a rising straight line. What calculation should represent that force’s work over the journey?
predict.defensible_answer: Add the separately signed areas of the flat and rising graph regions; one constant-force product cannot represent the entire varying segment.

attempt.produces: For the ground-frame body moving right x=0→5 m, force +3 N from x=0→2 m and then linearly +3→+9 N over x=2→5 m: identify target, force and frame; draw/describe the graph pieces; calculate each contribution, signed total and units; explain why using the starting height over all 5 m would or would not suffice.
attempt.model_response: Body is target, chosen force acts on it; +x right in ground frame. First rectangle W=3×2=+6 J. Next trapezium W=[(3+9)/2]×3=+18 J. Total +24 J. The starting 3 N across 5 m would give 15 J and miss the rising part. N·m=J.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the given force, body, ground frame, x endpoints and directed displacement.
rubric.evidence_of: Named force on body; right-positive ground frame, 0→5 m.

rubric.criterion: Computes separate rectangle and trapezium areas and signed total.
Includes a checked constant-height comparison and work units.

accepted: A correctly labelled two-region signed area yields +24 J.
rejected: Using the beginning 3 N over 5 m gives +15 J, which must be the total work. Incorrect: a later sloping section adds extra area beyond the starting rectangle.

route.ask: What is the target body and which force component is plotted?
route.why_this_ask: Prevents combining an unspecified different force.

route.ask: What shapes are present across the two position intervals?
route.why_this_ask: Makes the learner choose the representation before obtaining a result.

route.ask: Which signed contributions does each shape represent?
route.why_this_ask: Builds a checkable total.

route.ask: How can the one-height shortcut be independently tested?
route.why_this_ask: Tests the failure of endpoint force multiplication.

reconstruct.differs_from_teaching_path: Learner identifies and constructs pieces before seeing the area decomposition; Core1A displayed its decomposition.

boundary_test.prompt: If the rising second section became exactly horizontal at +3 N, what would the work from x=0→5 m be?
boundary_test.answer: +15 J from a single 3 N × 5 m rectangle; constant-force rule becomes valid.
boundary_test.confirms: Restores WEP-01 as a limiting case.

predict.prompt: A puck continues moving right while one force-component graph changes from above the horizontal x-axis to below it. Is the amount of work necessarily the sum of two positive geometric magnitudes?
predict.defensible_answer: No; for rightward motion the below-axis region contributes negative work and the areas add algebraically.

attempt.produces: For a puck in the ground frame moving right from x=1→5 m, a named force varies linearly from +8 N at x=1 to zero at x=3 and then −6 N at x=5. State body, force, direction and endpoints; break the graph into regions, compute signed works and their total in joules, and explain whether force=0 at x=3 requires the puck to stop.
attempt.model_response: The named force acts on the puck; ground +x right; puck traverses 1→5 m. Above-axis 1→3 triangle is +(½)(2)(8)=+8 J. Below-axis 3→5 triangle is −(½)(2)(6)=−6 J. Signed total = +2 J. Instantaneous force of this agent is 0 at x=3, which does not imply zero speed or zero accumulated work; other forces may act.

rubric.criterion: States target, force, ground frame, direction and endpoints.
rubric.evidence_of: Puck, named horizontal force, rightward 1→5 m.

rubric.criterion: Separates sign-changing graph into two signed regions and computes both.
Adds the signed works and distinguishes zero force from zero motion.
rubric.evidence_of: Net work by that force +2 J; no conclusion that the puck stops at x=3.

accepted: The single force does +2 J across the sign change; movement is stipulated.
rejected: Both triangles count positive because area is always positive; the total is +14 J. Incorrect: the below-axis piece counts −6 J in a rightward traversal.

route.ask: Which way does the body travel?
route.why_this_ask: Sets orientation of each work sign.

route.ask: Where does the given graph cross its zero-height line?
route.why_this_ask: Identifies independent regions before arithmetic.

route.ask: How do you record each region before addition?
route.why_this_ask: Elicits signed rather than unsigned accumulation.

route.ask: What does one instantaneous force value establish about speed?
route.why_this_ask: Separates force value from motion state.

reconstruct.differs_from_teaching_path: Learner must discriminate cancellation and motion first; Core1A made the sign-region solution visible.

boundary_test.prompt: If equal-magnitude triangles of opposite sign occur while the puck still moves right, what is the work of this named force?
boundary_test.answer: Zero signed total even though the force is nonzero over most of the motion and the puck moves.
boundary_test.confirms: Cancellation does not require no force or no motion.

predict.prompt: A named force has a negative signed component at both endpoints of a rightward displacement, but its magnitude changes. What must be considered before deciding the sign and amount of work?
predict.defensible_answer: The force component, its signed graph region, and directed displacement decide the work; the sign is negative for rightward travel here.

attempt.produces: For a body moving right from x=0→2 m in the ground frame, one force changes linearly from F_x=−3 N to −7 N. State the directed displacement, compute its signed work from a labelled geometric shape with units and calculate the work by the same force on an immediate x=2→0 return through the unchanged field.
attempt.model_response: From x=0→2 m the signed trapezium is [(−3−7)/2]×2=−10 J. On the reverse 2→0 traversal of the same force field, work is +10 J. This is work of the named force only; N·m=J.

rubric.criterion: Identifies directed displacement and relevant graph shape.
Computes correctly signed work in joules.
Calculates reversed-interval work under unchanged force field.

accepted: Forward work −10 J; reverse work +10 J.
rejected: Returning through the same negative graph also produces −10 J. Incorrect: reversed displacement changes the sign of each work contribution.

route.ask: What is the direction of each traversal?
route.why_this_ask: Secures the sign before numerical area.

route.ask: What geometric region is bounded by the two signed endpoint heights?
route.why_this_ask: Prompts model choice.

route.ask: What stays the same and what reverses on the return?
route.why_this_ask: Prevents treating the path as undirected.

reconstruct.differs_from_teaching_path: Core1B asks learner to compare directed travel against a fixed field rather than copying Core1A’s negative trapezium numbers.

boundary_test.prompt: If the force graph is identically F_x=0 over the two-metre forward displacement, what are both works?
boundary_test.answer: Both zero, despite the nonzero displacement.
boundary_test.confirms: A force component of zero gives zero work regardless of travel direction.

predict.prompt: An ideal anchored spring is stretched from one nonzero extension to a larger one. Does the extra work by an external balancing pull necessarily equal the entire stored energy at the final extension?
predict.defensible_answer: No. The incremental work depends on the change in stored spring energy, not its full final value; compare both endpoint extensions.

attempt.produces: An ideal spring k=150 N/m has attached body x1=+0.20 m and x2=+0.40 m; positive x is extension to right in the ground frame. The body is moved slowly with negligible friction, no other along-axis forces, and no appreciable change in K. Name spring and applied forces, state directed motion, find both endpoint force components, determine spring work and external balancing work with signs and units, and compare initial/final spring energy values.
attempt.model_response: Spring force on attached body F_s=−kx: F_s(.20)=−30 N and F_s(.40)=−60 N. Rightward stretch Δx=.20 m means W_spring=[(−30−60)/2](.20)=−9 J. With slow frictionless balance, applied agent does +9 J. U_initial=½(150)(.20²)=3 J; U_final=½(150)(.40²)=12 J; increase +9 J, not all 12 J. Units N·m=J.

rubric.criterion: Names target, forces, frame, spring coordinates and stated slow frictionless model.
rubric.evidence_of: Spring on body F_s=−kx, applied balancing pull opposite, x=.20→.40.

rubric.criterion: Computes the endpoint force components and signed work by the spring.
Computes applied work and both endpoint stored energies, with units.
rubric.evidence_of: Applied +9 J; U_i=3 J; U_f=12 J; ΔU=9 J.

accepted: The extra stretch requires +9 J of applied work and produces −9 J of spring work.
rejected: Since final spring energy is 12 J, the extra pull from .20 to .40 m must do +12 J. Incorrect: 3 J was already stored initially, so added work is +9 J.

route.ask: Which body moves and which agents exert opposing forces?
route.why_this_ask: Clarifies spring versus applied work.

route.ask: Which two heights on the spring-force graph bound this motion?
route.why_this_ask: Constructs the area interval.

route.ask: What should be compared at the two endpoint deformations?
route.why_this_ask: Elicits the nonzero-initial reference.

route.ask: Which assumptions let the external work be opposite spring work?
route.why_this_ask: Requires conditions instead of automatic sign transfer.

reconstruct.differs_from_teaching_path: Core1B requires the learner to construct agents, conditions and endpoint difference; Core1A showed an entirely different nonzero stretch.

boundary_test.prompt: If x2=x1 and the spring does not change position, what work is done by spring and balancing pull over that interval?
boundary_test.answer: Both zero: zero displacement gives zero work even if the spring is stretched and exerts force.
boundary_test.confirms: Separates nonzero spring force from work over a zero-length interval.

predict.prompt: An ideal spring end moves from compression through its relaxed length to extension. Can the spring’s total work be decided just by saying it always restores toward x=0?
predict.defensible_answer: No. Spring force points toward x=0, but its work depends on whether displacement aligns or opposes it on each portion.

attempt.produces: In a fixed ground frame, an ideal spring with k=80 N/m acts on a body that moves right from signed deformation x1=−0.30 m to x2=+0.10 m. Identify body, force and position signs; determine spring force at both endpoints and at zero, split the path at x=0, calculate the two signed triangular works and total spring work in joules; state whether any external balancing-work value follows without more assumptions.
attempt.model_response: For spring ON body F_s=−80x. At x=−0.30, +24 N; at 0, 0 N; at +0.10, −8 N. Rightward motion from −.30→0 gives +½(.30)(24)=+3.6 J, from 0→+.10 gives −½(.10)(8)=−0.4 J, sum W_s=+3.2 J. Neither slow motion nor negligible extra along-axis forces was stipulated; external work is undetermined from these data alone.

rubric.criterion: Declares ground frame, named spring-on-body force and signed endpoints.
Computes force values at negative, zero and positive deformations.
Splits traversal into signed triangles and adds work with units.
Distinguishes known spring work from unspecified external work.
rubric.evidence_of: External-agent work cannot be inferred without extra force/motion conditions.

accepted: Spring does +3.2 J over the traverse; external work unspecified.
rejected: The spring always opposes motion so both triangles are negative and total is −4.0 J. Incorrect: when compressed at negative x, restoring force points right with the rightward motion.

route.ask: Where is the spring’s undeformed reference?
route.why_this_ask: Draws the domain crossing.

route.ask: Which direction does the spring push at compressed versus stretched positions?
route.why_this_ask: Reconstructs the force law physically.

route.ask: What areas lie on each side of the zero-force crossing?
route.why_this_ask: Forces signed area selection.

route.ask: What additional conditions would be needed to assign a balancing external agent’s work?
route.why_this_ask: Distinguishes a force ledger from a motion-state assumption.

reconstruct.differs_from_teaching_path: Learner reconstructs the spring sign across zero and asks about unspecified external work; Core1A showed a separate spring with different deformations.

boundary_test.prompt: If the body returns from +0.10 m to −0.30 m through the same ideal spring law, what is its spring work?
boundary_test.answer: −3.2 J, the negative of the forward work; the closed out-and-back spring work is zero.
boundary_test.confirms: Reversibility and sign under reversed traversal.

predict.prompt: A body travels over a position-dependent force field and then reverses exactly along the same path. If the force law stays fixed, must work of that force over the return have the same sign as on the outward trip?
predict.defensible_answer: No. Work of an unchanged position-dependent force changes sign when the directed position interval reverses.

attempt.produces: A body moves in the fixed ground frame first x=1→4 m and then x=4→1 m. A named force on it is linearly F_x=2x N when x is in metres (equivalently 2 N/m times x) across the interval. State body, force, fixed-axis and directed intervals; compute work of that force on both legs by a labelled trapezium, give signs and units; check the total over the two legs.
attempt.model_response: F_x(1)=+2 N and F_x(4)=+8 N. Work x=1→4 m is [(2+8)/2]×3=+15 J. Reversed 4→1 m has −15 J because displacement direction reverses. Total work of this same force over the round trip =0 J. No claim about other forces is made.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the named force, body, fixed frame and both directed intervals.
Uses signed geometric trapezium with correct endpoint force values.
Reverses the sign and checks round-trip total including units.

accepted: +15 J outward, −15 J return, 0 J full trip.
rejected: Because the same graph is used twice, the return also does +15 J and the round-trip work is +30 J. Incorrect: the reversal of displacement reverses each contribution.

route.ask: What stays fixed on both legs?
route.why_this_ask: Identifies force law and reference axis.

route.ask: How is the same graph region traversed each time?
route.why_this_ask: Makes path orientation explicit.

route.ask: What relation should hold between work totals for a fixed field on reversed traversals?
route.why_this_ask: Boundary confirmation of signed area.

reconstruct.differs_from_teaching_path: Learner reasons about a reversed directed interval and returns, a task not used as a solved standalone A anchor.

boundary_test.prompt: If outward and return legs have different forces because an external controller changes the force law during the turn, does cancellation necessarily hold?
boundary_test.answer: No. The same-field assumption is essential; different force laws need separate work calculations.
boundary_test.confirms: Restricts the reversal check to an unchanged force law.

self_check_what_could_be_wrong: The learner might not distinguish signed oriented work from unsigned geometric area when traversing toward decreasing x.
A renderer could expose deferred equations/model answers before a genuine attempt.
External balancing-force work is not necessarily −spring work if movement is not quasi-static or extra dissipative work exists.
A diagram may be rendered with force agent/direction mislabelled even if its text description is correct.
The spring graph assumes a linear elastic range and ignores hysteresis, which may not hold for real springs.
Several similar triangular-area constructions could reduce diversity of pedagogical transfer.
Validation cannot substitute for independent physics or Grade 9 pedagogy review.
